thread.title: Amazon to Join Trillion-Dollar Club as Analyst Sees Stock Surging to $2,500

author: Barron's
title: Amazon to Join Trillion-Dollar Club as Analyst Sees Stock Surging to $2,500
text:
Courtesy of Amazon Could Amazon.com join Apple in the exclusive trillion-dollar club?
Morgan Stanley thinks so, and then some.
Based on 478 million shares outstanding, we calculate that Amazon 's ( AMZN ) stock price would have to hit $2,092.05 - about 8.2% above Tuesday's close of $1,932.82 -for the company's market capitalization to reach $1 billion.
In one of the most bullish reports to date on the e-commerce and cloud-computing behemoth, analyst Brian Nowak says Amazon could zoom to a $1.2 trillion valuation. He reiterated an Overweight rating on the stock and lifted the price target to $2,500 from $1,850, implying a whopping 29% upside to Tuesday's closing price.
"We have increasing confidence that Amazon's rapidly growing, increasingly large, high-margin revenue streams (advertising, AWS, subscriptions) will drive higher profitability and continued upward estimate revisions," Nowak wrote in a note to clients Wednesday.
Morgan Stanley's vote of confidence - its price target is the highest among 41 analysts who cover Amazon, according to FactSet - sent shares of Amazon up 2.4% to $1,978.60 in mid-morning trading today. The company's stock has surged 69% so far this year.
Nowak predicts that Amazon Web Services , paid subscriptions, and advertising will generate almost $45 billion in profit by 2020 from an estimated $25 billion this year. He also noted Amazon outperformed the top end of its operating-profit guidance by an average of 60% the past three quarterly reports.
At $942.7 billion, Amazon's market cap is second only to Apple ( AAPL ) in market value. The iPhone and iPad maker, which became the first public company to surpass $1 trillion in value in early August , is currently worth $1.1 trillion.
